text:
Samir Patel: billing-bot just fired a high-severity alert — $30k+ GPU usage spike in us-west1 in the last hour :warning:
billing-bot: [ALERT] project:redwood-prod - unexpected spend jump detected (gpu instances). link: https://billing.example/reports/193321
oncall-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-193321 (auto-tag: cost)
Maria Chen: looking... I see ~420 GPU vms launched across 3 zones (us-west1-a/b/c) starting ~1933200000
Kevin O'Neill: quick hypothesis: autoscaler picked the wrong nodepool. We have 2 GPU pools — gpu-reserved (CUD-attached, preferred) and gpu-ephemeral (no commitment). If requests couldn't satisfy constraints it can spill into gpu-ephemeral
Samir Patel: did we change any nodeSelector/nodeAffinity rules in the rollout last night? I remember a change to the gke node template
Maria Chen: yes, there's a recent terraform change to module/gke/node_pool: removed label "cud:yes" from gpu-reserved by accident. autoscaler policy prefers pools with label but fallback exists
Jen Park: also noticed the autoscaler policy has a weak matching block — priority: prefer pool with label but minCpu/taints didn't match, so it launched in gpu-ephemeral
Kevin O'Neill: the kicker: our committed use discounts are regional and tied to specific machine family + labels. Instances in gpu-ephemeral are different family (a2 -> a100) vs gpu-reserved (a2 -> a10x). So CUDs didn't apply
Maria Chen: digging through logs. gke-autoscaler logs show this: ```json
{"timestamp":1933209001,"reason":"capacity_constraint","selectedPool":"gpu-ephemeral","requestedGPU":"a100-v2"}
```
Maria Chen: created list of offending instances: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels.autoscale-start>1933208000 AND tags:gpu-ephemeral" --format="table(name,zone,machineType,creationTimestamp)"`
Samir Patel: oh no — some of these are even provisioned into a different project (host-project mismatch) — that would definitely break our CUD coverage
Kevin O'Neill: that explains the $30k. If instances are in wrong project, reservations/commitments don't apply. Did the template's serviceProject field change?
Jen Park: terraform change 1721 shows module.gke.node_pool.serviceProject = "redwood-other" instead of null — manual merge gone wrong during the infra merge
Samir Patel: OK immediate plan: 1) stop autoscaler, 2) scale down gpu-ephemeral pool to zero where safe, 3) migrate workloads/backfill to gpu-reserved after restoring labels, 4) open billing dispute/support case for retroactive coverage and ask for credits
Maria Chen: I'm doing step 2 now: `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-ephemeral --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=0 --cluster=prod-cluster`
Kevin O'Neill: I'll rollback the terraform change and add a validation check to the pipeline: fail if node_pool.serviceProject != production_project or missing label "cud:yes"
Jen Park: I'll open a support ticket with cloud (case 987654) and request quota/commitment reconciliation and ask if they can apply regional CUDs to the mis-provisioned instances retroactively
finance-bot: preliminary overage calc: approx $36,700 in uncommitted GPU hours for the window 1933200000-1933214000. Confirming details with billing export
Maria Chen: scaling down now, starting gradual cordon+drain on non-critical nodes. will post progress.
Samir Patel: also add guard in autoscaler config: require nodepool label match for GPU workloads (hard requirement, not prefer). This'll prevent future fallthroughs
Kevin O'Neill: adding terraform plan change: enforce nodepool labels and add pre-deploy check script: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
if ! terraform plan | grep -q "labels = { .*cud: \"yes\" }"; then
  echo "Missing cud label"; exit 1
fi
```
Jen Park: finance wants estimate for next bill to decide if we should dip into committed spare capacity for this month — cc @finance
finance-bot: flagging finance ops to review. estimated net impact after potential credits: $12k - $28k depending on support outcome
Samir Patel: thanks team. Maria/Kevin/Jen own remediation. I'll follow up in incident channel once we have rollback + support response. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: done cordon/scale down, currently draining 180 instances. will monitor new autoscaler events closely
Kevin O'Neill: pushed terraform rollback and pipeline check, patch in PR: #4123
Jen Park: support case submitted, requested expedited review and retroactive application of regional commitments. attached logs + instance list
Samir Patel: great. postmortem later with root cause: terraform mis-merge + weak autoscaler fallback policy + placement project mismatch -> uncommitted / wrong-family GPUs launched -> billing spike
Maria Chen: adding temporary alert: if >50 GPUs launched into non-cud pool in 10m, page oncall.
Samir Patel: ok closing this thread for now. Thanks everyone.
